name: CreateHatch
formula: =LAMBDA(vertices,[numberOfLines],[angleInDegree],LET(numLines, IF(ISOMITTED(numberOfLines), 10, numberOfLines), angle, IF(ISOMITTED(angleInDegree), RADIANS(45), RADIANS(angleInDegree)), vertical, ABS(COS(angle)) < 0.000000001, m, IF(vertical, NA(), TAN(angle)), n, ROWS(vertices), Cs, MAP(SEQUENCE(n), LAMBDA(i, LET(x, INDEX(vertices, i, 1), y, INDEX(vertices, i, 2), IF(vertical, x, y - m * x)))), minC, MIN(Cs), maxC, MAX(Cs), spacingC, (maxC - minC) / (numLines + 1), sequenceC, SEQUENCE(numLines, 1, minC + spacingC, spacingC), intersections, DROP(REDUCE(0, sequenceC, LAMBDA(acc,C, LET(cIntersections, {ref}PolySlopeIntersection(vertices, m, C), IF(ROWS(cIntersections) = 1, acc, VSTACK(acc, cIntersections))))), 1), numIntersections, ROWS(intersections) / 2, intersectionsForPlot, DROP(REDUCE(0, SEQUENCE(numIntersections, 1, 1, 2), LAMBDA(acc,i, LET(rows, CHOOSEROWS(intersections, i, i + 1), emptyRow, MAKEARRAY(1, 2, LAMBDA(r,c, NA())), VSTACK(acc, rows, emptyRow)))), 1), intersectionsForPlot))
comment: Returns hatch segments for a closed polygon, with a blank row between segments so a scatter chart breaks the line. vertices is an n×2 array of (x, y) rows in order; the last vertex connects to the first. numberOfLines defaults to 10. angleInDegree defaults to 45. Lines are spaced strictly between the extreme intercepts, so each line meets a convex polygon twice. A vertical angle uses a vertical line. Each segment is two (x, y) rows followed by #N/A. Fewer than two columns returns #REF!. A non-numeric coordinate returns #VALUE!. Last Update at 2026-11-03.
